- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) and forecast is trending up, reduce upward bias — model tends to overreact to sentiment.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) and forecast is trending down, avoid excessive downward correction — model underreacts to bearish sentiment.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >70.5), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days — apply a 1–2% downward correction to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon — if forecast is >1.5σ above recent mean, adjust downward; if <1.5σ below, adjust upward.
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., 0.50–0.67) correlate with 1–2 day lagged price moves — model should anticipate sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead, not react immediately.
- In 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates upward momentum after sentiment peaks — add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast if sentiment >0.50 in last 3 days.
